source.note: Hypertension: 'usual initial dosage is 100 mg daily in single or divided doses ... effective dosage range of Lopressor tablets is 100 mg to 450 mg per day.' Modeled as twice-daily (12 h) dosing, so per-dose = half the daily amount: min 50 mg, typical 50 mg (initial), max 225 mg.
'The estimated oral bioavailability of immediate release metoprolol is about 50%'

'The mean elimination half-life of metoprolol is 3 to 4 hours; in poor CYP2D6 metabolizers the half-life may be 7 to 9 hours.' model = midpoint of the normal-metabolizer range; poor metabolizers (~8% of Caucasians, ~2% of other groups) run longer.
'Metoprolol is extensively distributed with a reported volume of distribution of 3.2 to 5.6 L/kg.' model = midpoint of the label range (curve value; change if you prefer another)

source.citation: Health Canada Product Monograph: PrMETOPROLOL (Metoprolol Tartrate Tablets USP), Pro Doc Ltée, revised 2021-08-17, p.22 (Pharmacokinetics – Absorption)
source.note: US Lopressor label (12.3) gives no Tmax number. Monograph: 'Peak plasma concentrations are attained after approximately 1.5 to 2 hours with conventional metoprolol formulations.' model = midpoint of the range.
'Lopressor is primarily metabolized by CYP2D6 ... Poor CYP2D6 metabolizers exhibit several-fold higher plasma concentrations of Lopressor than extensive metabolizers'
'LOPRESSOR is indicated for the treatment of hypertension in adult patients, to lower blood pressure.'

'Approximately 95% of the dose can be recovered in urine. In most subjects (extensive metabolizers), less than 5% of an oral dose ... are excreted as unchanged drug in the urine.' unchanged_fraction uses the stated <5% upper bound for extensive metabolizers; poor metabolizers may excrete up to 30-40% unchanged.

journey.text: Taken by mouth and absorbed from the gut; the liver breaks down about half of each dose before it reaches the rest of the body.
Broken down in the liver, mainly by the CYP2D6 enzyme. People whose CYP2D6 works slowly build up higher levels.
Blocks beta-1 receptors in the heart, slowing the heart rate and easing its workload, which lowers blood pressure.
Leaves the body in urine within about a day, mostly as broken-down pieces rather than unchanged drug.
